items.title: How much does weighting change the winner?
items.description: This uses L3's Kafka-vs-NATS-vs-Hosted-SQS sub-scores directly. Drag 'Weight on migration cost' to see how much the winning candidate depends on how heavily the team values cheap, fast adoption versus the other criteria (the remaining weight is split evenly across familiarity, maturity, and strategic fit). At the default 30%, Hosted SQS wins by a comfortable margin — the same conclusion L3 reaches with its own hand-picked weights.
items.compute: const mcw = params.migrationCostWeight / 100; const rest = (1 - mcw) / 3; const w = { familiarity: rest, maturity: rest, migrationCost: mcw, strategicFit: rest }; const candidates = [ { name: 'Kafka', familiarity: 3, maturity: 9, migrationCost: 2, strategicFit: 5 }, { name: 'NATS', familiarity: 5, maturity: 6, migrationCost: 6, strategicFit: 7 }, { name: 'Hosted SQS', familiarity: 8, maturity: 8, migrationCost: 8, strategicFit: 6 } ]; const score = (c) => c.familiarity * w.familiarity + c.maturity * w.maturity + c.migrationCost * w.migrationCost + c.strategicFit * w.strategicFit; return { kafkaScore: score(candidates[0]), natsScore: score(candidates[1]), sqsScore: score(candidates[2]) };

items.title: How stale does a radar get between reviews?
items.description: L2's chart showed staleness rising as review frequency drops. This lets you explore the same relationship with a real variable: how fast the team's stack is actually changing. A team using stable, slow-moving technology can tolerate a longer gap between reviews than one adopting new tools constantly.
items.compute: const staleness = Math.min(100, params.reviewGapMonths * params.changeRate * 2.2); return { staleness };
